Scientific questions, small models, and the evidence behind predictions. A practical course for master's students in chemistry, taught by Kevin Maik Jablonka.

## Next class: 11 November

**12:10–16:00 · Helmholtzweg 4, SR 6 Physik.** We start with our first Python notebook, then work through an ML MolSim lecture on training, kernels, standardisation, and testing. The MOF notebook is available throughout, with time to work together in class and continue on 2 December. Bring your laptop, charger, and any setup questions.

## How we work {#how-to-use-a-lecture-page}

Short explanations lead into calculations you can inspect, change, and discuss. Unfinished attempts are welcome. We will collect project ideas in a shared document; its link will be sent to the class by email. The [assessment](outline.qmd#assessment) combines a project report and a presentation with discussion; deadlines are still to be agreed.

[]{#feedback}

Tell me what helped you understand something and what got in the way. Your feedback helps me adjust the next session.

## About these notes {#about-these-notes}

I develop these materials in iterative dialogue with OpenAI's Codex, drawing on earlier teaching and the sources cited in the notes. I direct the course and remain responsible for its content, including errors. Our aim is to use assistants while retaining judgement about the question, calculation, and evidence.
